facts.text: Lake Lynn grew around a 1926 hydroelectric dam built by West Penn Power, which flooded the Cheat River valley to create the lake that now bears its name.
Lake Lynn sits at 886 feet above sea level on the Cheat River, just 2 miles east-southeast of Point Marion and right on the Pennsylvania–West Virginia line.
The area that became Lake Lynn was first settled by Scotch‑Irish and German families after the Revolutionary War, who logged timber and farmed the rolling hills of Springhill Township.
Lake Lynn’s climate is humid continental, with average January highs around 35°F and July highs near 83°F, while snowfall averages 32 inches each winter.
The Cheat River, a tributary of the Monongahela, dominates Lake Lynn’s hydrology, and its dam releases control seasonal water levels that shape the local ecosystem.
